# dsh-btw-marginalia
> Read-only side questions for DeepSeek Harness. Ask in the margin, keep the main thread clean.

`marginalia` (noun): notes written in the margin of a page. That is what `/btw` is in
oh-my-pi: a no

te taken beside the main conversation,
without changing it.
This is a DSH Host + Web Client bundle that implements the practical form of that contract:

- **Same conversation** — the side turn forks the current session, so it sees the same system
prompt

, the same tool catalog, and the same completed history.
- **Read-only, enforced** — the inherited t

ools remain in the request to preserve the prompt
prefix, but an execution-time guard rejects every

tool call. This is not a prompt request.
- **Visible in-flight context** — while the main turn is ru

nning, the side prompt gets a compact,
capped snapshot of the current user request, recent tool call

s/results, and the live assistant
partial. This is what makes first-turn `/btw` useful even before `

turn/end`.
- **Topics and history** — every question is persisted with its status and answer; follow

-ups
replay the topic and see the parent conversation as it is *now*.
- **Streaming and cancellation

** — the Web Client retains the child session, renders its partial
text, and preserves what was gene

rated when you stop it.
- **No fabricated branch** — DSH has no public "insert an assistant message

/ create a branch"
API. Marginalia does not pretend; it offers **insert into composer** as the safe

ranch"
API. Marginalia does not pretend; it offers **insert into composer** as the safe replacement.
## Screenshots
The real /btw slash entry · streaming in the margin, with Stop and insert actions
Topic history with follow-up · light and dark DSH themes

Screenshots are produced by the Playwright screenshot spec (`npm run screenshots`) against an
isolat
ed Host and a deterministic demo model, not by hand-editing the UI.
## Requirements

- DSH `>= 0.2.1-rc.1 < 0.3.0-0` (tested against `0.2.1-rc.2`)
- Node `>= 22`
- Works on a plain-HTTP
LAN Web GUI: `crypto.randomUUID` is restricted to secure contexts, so the plugin uses `getRandomVal

ues` (or a non-cryptographic identifier fallback) when needed.
- A composed `fork` subagent provider

and `storage-domain` for durable history
(both are part of the standard Web profile; the plugin fal

ls back to process memory if the
storage domain is absent)
- For the browser suite: `dsh` on `PATH`
(or `DSH_BIN`), `pnpm`, and Playwright Chromium + Firefox
## Install
### Into a DSH profile
[代码示例省略，未执行]

A git-hosted install builds the bundle once; DSH asks you to approve that build script
(`allowBuilds
`) before it runs. The published package installs prebuilt and skips that step:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## How it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The public `/btw` command is contributed by an `inputTriggers` slash source, not by patching the
off

icial command UI. Bubbles use `conversation.input.overlay`; history uses `shell.overlay`; the
toolba

r button uses `conversation.input.left`. The host-side compatibility shims hide the internal
transpo

rt commands from the slash directory and drop their `command/run`/`command/done` lifecycle
pair, so
the main transcript and session log stay clean.

See `docs/architecture.md` for the full design and
`docs/verification.md` for what has and has not b

itecture.md` for the full design and
`docs/verification.md` for what has and has not been exercised.
## Security properties

- No HTTP routes. All reads/writes go through the authenticated `commands.execute` RPC.
- The side c

hild can never execute a tool, including `send_message`.
- No raw HTML, remote images, or sanitized

Markdown extensions are rendered in answers.
- Host errors are reduced to one bounded, control-chara

cter-free line.
- The plugin refuses to start from a subagent view; side questions are a main-sessio

n feature.
- Child sessions inherit the parent's sandbox/permission model; the guard only removes to

ol
execution, it does not widen permissions.
## Honest limitations

- **Not truly ephemeral.** A local fork creates a durable child session. Marginalia archives it
afte

r completion when the workspace registry is available; it cannot make the Host forget it.
History it

self is stored in a sidecar domain.
- **No branch.** DSH exposes no public assistant-message injecti

on/branch API. The `b` behavior of
oh-my-pi is intentionally not imitated.
- **History replay is tex

t, not role-level messages.** The child receives one user prompt with a
`<btw-history>` section. Rol

e-level replay would require a direct LLM call and would lose the
fork's system/tools/cache inherita

nce.
- **Prompt cache is preserved, not guaranteed.** Marginalia never changes system/tools/messages

;
the completed-turn prefix can be reused, but the current open-turn snapshot is new text, so it is

necessarily outside that cache. Whether a provider reuses the prefix remains its decision.
- **Open-

turn context is best-effort and snapshot-based.** Fork cannot seed an unbalanced turn, so
Marginalia

injects the current task/tool/partial snapshot itself. It is capped, taken when you
ask, and may be

stale if the main turn advances while the side answer is generated.
- **Archive is best-effort.** A

failed archive is logged; the side history is still correct.
- **Transport is still command RPC.**

The lifecycle shim removes transcript/log pollution, but the
internal commands remain directly calla

ble by an authorized RPC client. A generated Remote
namespace would be cleaner; it is not implemente

d yet.
- **Subagent view is not in the browser suite.** Unit tests cover the refusal and hidden tool

e is gated.** `real.nightly.spec.ts` is skipped unless
`DSH_E2E_REAL=1` and `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` are s

s gated.** `real.nightly.spec.ts` is skipped unless
`DSH_E2E_REAL=1` and `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` are set.
